definition: A table used to evaluate classification models by showing counts of true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives.
details: Confusion matrices allow computation of derived metrics like precision, recall, and F1 score, and help diagnose specific types of model errors.
story: Picture a scoreboard at a science fair: you need a fair, agreed way to tell who actually won. Here is the short version: A table used to evaluate classification models by showing counts of true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives. The part that makes it sing: Confusion matrices allow computation of derived metrics like precision, recall, and F1 score, and help diagnose specific types of model errors. A good metric is a ruler that does not bend when you lean on it. And that, done honestly, is Confusion Matrix.
